top_signals.title: El Niño Could Push Up Food Prices in Southern Africa
top_signals.summary: Absa AgriBusiness agricultural economist Zama Sangweni says El Niño could reduce summer crop yields and put upward pressure on food prices. She explains how more severe weather could also reshape regional trade and why countries including Zambia may be especially exposed through agriculture, employment and hydropower. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Calls to Overhaul the UN Security Council Gain New Momentum
top_signals.summary: With Kyrgyzstan set to begin a two-year term on the UN Security Council at the end of this year, the Central Asian nation’s president, Sadyr Japarov, sent some barbs and props to President Donald Trump in a speech at the General Assembly. Japarov’s September 22 address made it clear that Bishkek sides with China on the matter of reforming the United Nations, with the aim of altering the balance of power within the institution to diminish Western influence.  “Today the world has changed,” Japarov stated. top_signals.title: Global Gas Squeeze Could Last Through Next Summer
top_signals.summary: Global natural gas supply is likely to remain tighter than it should be until next summer at least, and it could cause prolonged demand destruction. Should this scenario materialize, it would deliver a severe blow to Europe, as it already struggles to cover its winter gas needs ahead of the official start of heating season—but Asia won’t be happy about it, either.
